### 1. Overview

#### 1.1 Overview

This is a five-year project on rice farming in Thailand, targeting 21 provinces in the three most important rice-growing regions of the country: the north, the northeast and the east (see map). The project will be implemented by the Department of Agriculture for rice farming in Thailand. As such, it is a cross-cutting, medium-term project with a dual objective:

(a) To adapt rice farming in Thailand to order to reduce the negative impacts of observed and anticipated climate change conditions; and

(b) To reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions resulting from rice farming in order to help mitigate climate change.

## The Thai Rice Project Will

The Thai Rice Project will enable climate-smart rice farmers—increasingly, women farmers—to adapt to a changing climate (Outcome 1) while simultaneously reducing GHG emissions (Outcome 2).

### Project Design and Outcomes

#### Bottom-up Approach
- **Behavioral Changes**: Triggered at the level of the farmer through behavioral changes.
- **Adoption of Climate-smart Practices**: Climate-smart practices (Output 1.1) and climate-smart technologies will be made available by service providers—industrialized, mechanized, and well-equipped service providers supported by a strong institutional framework.

#### Financial Support
- The climate-smart rice that is produced will be verified and sold at higher market prices.
- A financial support mechanism will be established to ensure the sustainability of this sector, designed and implemented to unlock additional revenue flows to support Thailand’s transition towards a low-carbon economy (Outcome 3).

# GREEN CLIMATE FUND FUNDING PROPOSAL V10.0 | PAGE 48

## Barriers for Service Providers

### Climate-smart rice farming is at its nascent stage in Thailand: aspects of the emission and/or mitigation potential of climate-smart farming have been posted or synthesised, rolled-out by foundation projects, but baseline projects, but they have not been promoted and disseminated at a large scale nor in an integrated manner. The lack of awareness among farmers about the benefits of climate-smart technology and equipment carries substantial risk due to the unclear business case (particularly for smallholder farmers) compared with the well-established and well-understood sugar cane service provider sector. There is also a perception that the climate-smart rice service provision model is not financially viable, compared with the well-established and well-understood sugar cane service provider sector.

Dear Madam, Sir,

We refer to the project “Mitigating GHG emission through modern, efficient and climate friendly clean cooking solutions” in Nepal as included in the funding proposal submitted by Alternative Energy Promotion Center to us on 13 December 2020.

The undersigned is the duly authorized representative of Ministry of Finance, International Economic Cooperation Coordination Division (hereinafter referred to as “Designated Authority of Nepal”).

2. Proposed Interventions

To mitigate the impacts of climate change and strengthen resilience of the most vulnerable communities to adapt to climate change, Alternative Energy Promotion Centre (AEP) has proposed to implement the project "Mitigating GHG emission through modern, efficient and climate friendly clean cooking solutions (CCS)". The project will be implemented in Nepal by AEP with financial support from the Green Climate Fund. It aims at mitigating climate change impacts on vulnerable communities of Nepal by: (i) Introducing innovative concepts in Nepal of (ii) bulk tendering via reverse auctioning for cost effectiveness; (iii) output based financing for de-risking of investments and (iv) mainstreaming and capacitating local governments to ensure long-term sustainability. The project will be implemented in 10 districts across the country up to now and could be game changers in the clean cooking sector.

Furthermore, as per the Second NDC of Nepal, currently around 5% of households use electric induction stoves and this is expected to increase to 30% by 2030. The project contributes significantly to the achieve the target on the use of electric stoves. Strengthened supply chain, expansion of the manufacturing base in the country, will project, will proliferate across the country without external interventions even after the project period.

The project is a priority of the GoN and is linked to the Government-led national strategy on Forest Climate Change Programmes, which projects employment and adequate engagement of relevant stakeholders, which are aligned with national climate change priorities. This is a priority under the National Development Plan (NDP) 2017-23. The Ministry of Environment and Forests of Nepal has indicated this project as a priority for GCF. GoN of Nepal is providing about 65% co-financing to this project. The fifteen-year plan of the National Planning Commission envisions the expansion of clean cooking in Nepal, which includes the promotion of LPG stoves, biogas digesters, and bio briquettes and EGS. Annex B - Gender Assessment and Action Plan

1. Introduction: Relevance of Gender Mainstreaming for the Project

This Gender Assessment has been prepared as an input for the design of the Green Climate Fund (GCF) funding proposal by UN Environment Programme (UNEP), titled "Enhancing Early Warning Systems to build greater resilience to hydro-meteorological hazards in Timor-Leste". The project aims at building climate resilience and disaster preparedness capacities at national, sub-national and community level in Timor-Leste through the development of end-of-bend climate and oceans services and impact-based multi-hazard early warning systems. These systems will help communities that are most vulnerable to climate change impacts such as sea level rise, increasing mean temperatures and extreme climatic events, including droughts, floods, landslides, and cyclones.

# GREEN CLIMATE FUND FUNDING PROPOSAL V2.1 | PAGE 18 OF 116

B

## Project Results

### i) Strengthened delivery model and integration for integrated climate information and multi-hazard early warning systems (MHEWS) in Timor-Leste
The project will establish a national climate service (NCS) based on the GFCC to coordinate, facilitate and strengthen collaboration among national institutions for the development of an NCS. The NCS will be established as a focal point for the delivery of the multi-hazard business model of the national meteorological and hydrological service (DMG). Moreover, it will instigate a best practice approach to data governance and advance the integration of climate, health, agriculture, disaster risk reduction, water and environmental management sectors in Timor-Leste.

# GREEN CLIMATE FUND FUNDING PROPOSAL V2.1 PAGE 98 OF 110

## E

This Activity will build the capacity of Timor-Leste to prepare for and respond to the impacts of climate change risks and health impacts. The Project will work with the Civil Protection Unit (CPL) - Timor- Leste, the National Directorate for Climate Change (DNCC), and the National Directorate for Disaster Management (NDM) to enhance disaster preparedness through capacity building at national level for early warning systems (EWS) and community-level for disaster risk management and co-ordination.

In addition, The Project will conduct a targeted disaster risk awareness and education campaign for women, which will focus on empowering women with the understanding and knowledge for improved disaster risk management and decision-making for climate resilience.
